rules.title: Keep control flow direct and proportionate

triggers: new or materially changed functions, modules, or abstractions

rules.requirement: Changed code must use the simplest control flow and abstraction shape that preserves the governing invariants. Every additional branch, layer, wrapper, generic, or indirection must carry a concrete responsibility.
authoring_projection: State the invariant before adding a branch or abstraction.
Prefer a direct implementation when an extra layer has no independent policy, boundary, substitution, or evidence role.
Re-read the final diff for nested control flow and machinery that can be removed without hiding intent.

At closeout, account for every changed line and public trait implementation against requested behavior, a governing invariant, or necessary diagnostics. Remove optional derives, convenience surface, formatting-only churn, and boilerplate that the task or repository contract does not require.

mechanical_enforcement.check: clippy::complexity plus a repository-selected cognitive-complexity threshold
mechanical_enforcement.caveat: Lint success cannot prove that an abstraction is justified or readable.

remediation.guidance: Flatten control flow or remove machinery only after checking callers, public contracts, and the responsibility the structure may encode.

required_evidence: why the simpler shape is insufficient
focused test or contract evidence when risk-bearing

completion_evidence: recorded rationale for retained non-obvious structure

rules.title: Public types implement semantically appropriate common traits
rules.requirement: Every public type must implement Debug unless doing so would expose protected data. Other common traits must be implemented only when their semantics are valid and useful for the type.
authoring_projection: For each new public type, decide Debug first and then consider Clone, equality, ordering, hashing, display, default, and conversions by semantics.
Use a manual redacted Debug implementation when derived output would expose protected data.

mechanical_enforcement.caveat: The lint does not decide redaction or which other traits are semantically correct.

remediation.guidance: Add only justified derives or manual implementations; treat public trait additions as API decisions.

required_evidence: why Debug is unsafe or inapplicable
review of other applicable common traits

completion_evidence: compiler or lint evidence for Debug coverage

rules.title: Represent recoverable failure explicitly

triggers: fallible operations, untrusted input, external boundaries, unwrap, expect, panic, indexing

rules.requirement: Recoverable failures must be represented with Result, Option, or a repository-defined equivalent. Panics and panic-capable convenience operations are reserved for proven programming errors or explicit termination policy, with the invariant made visible.
authoring_projection: Classify each new failure as recoverable, programmer error, or process-fatal policy before choosing Result, Option, assertion, or panic.
At external and untrusted-input boundaries, propagate contextual errors instead of unwrap or expect.

mechanical_enforcement.check: selective clippy::unwrap_used, clippy::expect_used, clippy::panic, and clippy::indexing_slicing
mechanical_enforcement.caveat: Tests, const contexts, poisoned locks, and proven invariants require repository-specific policy; do not enable the restriction group wholesale.

action_overrides.reason: Defining or changing foreign error signaling, sentinel values, out-parameters, callbacks, or ABI status semantics changes the caller contract.

remediation.guidance: Propagate or translate recoverable errors with context. Retain a panic only when the violated programming invariant and termination intent are explicit.

completion_evidence: panic-capable site review for changed scope

rules.title: Unsafe code states and contains its proof obligations

triggers: unsafe block, unsafe function, unsafe trait or implementation, raw pointer, FFI boundary

rules.requirement: Every unsafe operation must be necessary, narrowly scoped, and preceded by a SAFETY explanation that discharges every documented precondition of that exact operation with concrete invariants. Public unsafe functions must document every caller obligation in a Safety section. Safe wrappers must uphold those obligations for every safe call.
authoring_projection: Use unsafe only after ruling out an established safe alternative.

Keep the block minimal. Check the exact unsafe API contract, discharge every documented precondition in the SAFETY comment, and expose every caller obligation in a Safety doc section; a generic validity claim is insufficient.

Before writing the proof, copy the operation's documented Safety bullets into a checklist. For pointer and range operations, explicitly resolve provenance and single-allocation, alignment, non-nullness, readable or writable initialized extent, aliasing and mutation for the full borrow, lifetime, termination, and length or offset bounds such as isize::MAX; mark non-applicable items instead of omitting them.

For CStr::from_ptr, separately state that the pointer has valid provenance, the complete range through the first NUL lies in one allocation, that range is initialized and readable, the terminator is within isize::MAX bytes, and the memory is not mutated for the returned borrow. Put caller obligations in the public Safety section and the operation-specific discharge immediately above the call.

At closeout, tick each copied Safety bullet only when the final public contract and operation-local proof state the concrete invariant that discharges it. Never infer provenance or single-allocation from a generic validity or readability claim.
Add risk-selected tests and analysis for the unsafe boundary.

mechanical_enforcement.caveat: A present comment may still be wrong; soundness requires manual invariant review and proportionate dynamic evidence.

remediation.guidance: Ordinary and strict audits must report and classify unsafe findings without changing the boundary. High-assurance repair additionally requires pinned official operation contracts and independent review evidence; stop for operator direction if either is absent or the safe API contract must change.

rules.title: Do not hold a non-async lock guard across suspension

triggers: await while a std::sync or parking_lot lock guard is live

rules.requirement: A non-async-aware mutex or read/write lock guard must not remain live across an await point.
authoring_projection: End the scope of every std::sync or parking_lot guard before awaiting.
Extract the minimum state, release the guard, perform async work, then reacquire only for a bounded update.

mechanical_enforcement.caveat: Explicit drop may produce a known false positive; use lexical scope and manually review state-consistency effects.

remediation.guidance: Shorten the guard's lexical scope. Do not mechanically swap lock types without reviewing contention, cancellation, and state consistency.

required_evidence: why the guard is not a blocking lock or why the lint is false

completion_evidence: concurrency test or stated reason it is unnecessary

rules.title: Honour the repository-declared Rust version

crate_kinds: all Cargo packages with a supported-version policy
triggers: language feature, standard-library API, dependency, edition, or lint whose availability varies by Rust release

rules.requirement: Code, dependencies, lints, and generated projections must compile and operate on the repository's declared minimum supported Rust version unless an explicit version-policy change is authorized.
authoring_projection: Read rust-version and repository toolchain policy before selecting syntax, APIs, lints, or dependencies.
Treat raising the MSRV as a compatibility decision, not an incidental cleanup.

mechanical_enforcement.check: build and test matrix at package rust-version; optional cargo-msrv evidence
mechanical_enforcement.caveat: The newest local compiler cannot prove compatibility with the declared minimum.

action_overrides.reason: Raising rust-version, changing edition or toolchain policy, or dropping a supported compiler changes the repository compatibility contract.

remediation.guidance: Prefer an equivalent supported construct. Stop before raising rust-version, changing the edition, or dropping a supported toolchain.

required_evidence: reason the declared toolchain cannot be exercised

completion_evidence: minimum-toolchain build or explicit blocked evidence
version-policy decision for any proposed raise

rules.title: Reject pass-through wrappers without an independent responsibility

triggers: function whose sole operation forwards the same arguments to another function

rules.requirement: A pass-through wrapper should exist only when it owns a stable API boundary, visibility boundary, substitution seam, policy, instrumentation point, type translation, or another named responsibility.
authoring_projection: Before adding a forwarding function, name the boundary or policy it owns.
Call the underlying operation directly when the wrapper has no independent responsibility.

mechanical_enforcement.caveat: The syntax detector cannot identify stable façades or architectural seams and must never auto-delete a wrapper.

remediation.guidance: This experimental candidate never authorizes mutation. Preserve a justified façade and record its responsibility. Delete a wrapper only when an independent normative rule supplies repair authority after caller and boundary review.

required_evidence: why direct use would weaken the boundary
